idiom_name: RxJS BehaviorSubject<State> + Subject<Event> with discriminated-union exhaustiveness
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds compile-time rigour to the same RxJS machinery used in JavaScript: events and states are discriminated unions, so a reducer's switch is checked for exhaustiveness and a missing case becomes a type error, while the component exposes dispatch(event: Event) and state$: Observable<State> backed by a BehaviorSubject or a scan pipeline with startWith and shareReplay(1). Where a single store is preferred, Redux Toolkit's createSlice documents the same contract with action objects as events and reducers as (state, action) => newState, and typed selectors replace hand-written subscriptions; React binds through useSyncExternalStore, Angular through signals or async pipes. Payloads crossing a network boundary must still be validated before they become events.
pitfalls: Types vanish at runtime: events built from JSON or any bypass the union, so validate at the boundary (zod, io-ts) before dispatch or the exhaustiveness guarantee is decorative.
BehaviorSubject is not equality-conflated: emitting an equivalent state object re-notifies every subscriber - add distinctUntilChanged or a shallow comparator.
Subscription leaks in components (React effects, Angular services) keep the store and its closures alive; return the unsubscribe from the effect or use the framework's binding.
Typed reducers invite side effects put in 'just this once' for convenience; I/O belongs in the handler layer, otherwise every test must mock the world.
